getting-started-connecting-the-bridge--d.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; # Connecting the Bridge (Claude Code ↔ Figma) The **S2A Toolkit** plugin can connect to **Claude Code** (or any MCP client) so an AI assistant can read and drive your Figma file — the same `figma_execute` workflow the design-infra team uses. This page gets you connected in three steps. The Bridge is **optional**. The toolkit's other features — component docs, annotations, variant filter, token release — work without it. ## How it fits together The toolkit plugin (in Figma) is the **Bridge client**. It connects over a local WebSocket to a small **MCP server** running on your machine, which your MCP client launches. We ship that server as a one-command launcher, **`@adobecom/s2a-toolkit-bridge`** (a pinned, known-good `figma-console-mcp`). ``` Claude Code ⇄ @adobecom/s2a-toolkit-bridge ⇄ S2A Toolkit plugin ⇄ your Figma file (MCP / stdio) (ws://localhost:9223–9232) ``` ## You need
  • Figma Desktop — the web app can't run the Bridge.
  • The S2A Toolkit plugin, installed from Adobe Enterprise in Figma.
  • An MCP client — Claude Code, Cursor, etc.
  • A Figma personal access token (starts with figd_) — create one here.
### Don't mix up the three tokens
TokenUsed for
Figma PAT (figd_…)The Bridge, to reach Figma. This page.
GitHub read:packagesOnly to npm install @adobecom/* packages.
GitHub PATOnly for running a token release from the toolkit.
## Step 1 — Point npm at GitHub Packages (once) In your `~/.npmrc`: ```ini @adobecom:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_TOKEN} ``` Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` in your environment (a `read:packages` token, authorized for the `adobecom` org). ## Step 2 — Add the Bridge server to your MCP client **Claude Code:** ```bash claude mcp add s2a-toolkit-bridge -s user \ -e FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN=figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE \ -- npx -y @adobecom/s2a-toolkit-bridge ``` **By hand** (Claude Code `.mcp.json`, Cursor `.cursor/mcp.json`, …): ```json { "mcpServers": { "s2a-toolkit-bridge": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@adobecom/s2a-toolkit-bridge"], "env": { "FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN": "figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" } } } } ``` Your MCP client launches the server on demand — nothing to start or manage yourself. ## Step 3 — Open the Bridge in Figma In **Figma Desktop**, open the **S2A Toolkit** plugin → **Bridge** tab. It scans ports `9223–9232` and connects to the running server. Claude Code can now read and drive your file. ## Troubleshooting
  • Bridge tab won't connect — make sure your MCP client has actually started the server (open Claude Code and use any Figma tool once), and that you're in Figma Desktop, not the browser.
  • Auth errors — the FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN must be a valid figd_… token; regenerate if unsure.
  • Port already in use — the server falls back across 9223–9232; the toolkit scans the same range, so a fallback port still connects.
